Quantities of a Quadratic Penalty for a Marginal Criterion

Derivatives for a marginal criterion

A Laplace approximation to a marginal likelihood differentiates the determinant of the penalized information, so it needs the hyperparameter derivatives of the coefficient Hessian and of the mixed block. The hyperparameters of a penalty that supplies them can be estimated by REML or ML. SCAD, MCP and a separable penalty with a kink do not supply them.

The quadratic branch

A fixed matrix P, an optional map D and one smoothing parameter lambda, so the penalty is the negative log-density of a Gaussian prior with precision lambda D’PD, improper when D’PD is singular. The rank, the null basis and the log pseudo-determinant are computed from D’PD when the object is built.

quadratic_penalty()
Construct a Quadratic Penalty
QuadraticPenalty()
S7 Class for the Quadratic Penalty

The additive branch

A sum of quadratic penalties with a smoothing parameter on each, which is the penalty of an anisotropic tensor-product smooth. The rank is computed at construction from the sum of the components after each component is divided by its largest absolute entry, because the null space of the sum does not depend on the smoothing parameters.

additive_penalty()
Construct a Sum of Quadratic Penalties
AdditivePenalty()
S7 Class for a Sum of Quadratic Penalties

The separable branch

The negative log-density of a continuous distributions7 family at the coordinates of the mapped coefficients, one coordinate at a time for a univariate family and one block at a time for a multivariate one. The lasso is a Laplace at zero, the elastic net is the product of a Laplace and a Gaussian, and the heavy-tailed prior is a Student t. The ridge, documented with them, is the Gaussian at zero written by its precision and is built on the quadratic branch.

The structured branch

A parameters7 matrix parameter used as the precision, so the hyperparameters are the free values of that structure and every derivative comes from its derivative arrays.

SCAD and MCP

Defined by their derivative rather than by a density. Their value is bounded, so exp(-value) is not integrable: they are improper, carry no normalizing constant and cannot come from a distribution.

scad_penalty() mcp_penalty()

ScadPenalty() McpPenalty()
S7 Classes for the SCAD and MCP Penalties

The proximal operator

The operator that a proximal gradient method applies after each gradient step: a linear solve for the quadratic and structured branches, a closed form for the Gaussian, Laplace, elastic-net, SCAD and MCP penalties, and a coordinatewise root for any other separable parent with a smooth log-density.
